item.title: Netdata provides real-time distributed observability with per-second AI anomaly detection
item.description:
Netdata provides real-time distributed observability with per-second AI anomaly detection

Netdata is a full-stack observability platform that covers infrastructure, application performance, digital experience, network performance, databases, logs, and cloud environments. The system is distributed and real-time, with its Agents collecting, storing, and analyzing data where it is generated every second.

🔍 Overview

Netdata monitors multiple layers of technology, including:

  • Infrastructure
  • Application performance monitoring (OpenTelemetry traces, service maps, RED)
  • Digital experience (real user monitoring, synthetic monitoring)
  • Network performance monitoring (SNMP, topology, NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow, traps, BGP)
  • Databases
  • Logs (monitoring and management)
  • Cloud
  • AI troubleshooting across all components

🧩 How it works

The architecture relies on data staying close to where it is created, stored in independent hubs placed where they make sense. Netdata Agents collect, store, and analyze data locally per second, applying machine learning anomaly detection on every metric. Netdata Parents and Netdata Cloud then combine these data points into a single view without centralizing the data itself. Because every piece of data gets its meaning at the time of collection, dashboards build themselves and ensure every chart is correct. Every metric is scored for anomalies every second, allowing clusters of anomalies to reveal hidden dependencies and show how problems cascade across systems, networks, and applications.

⚙️ Key details

  • Cost Engineering: Netdata collects everything every second and engineers the cost down to about 0.6 bytes per sample, making it unnecessary to choose what to watch.
  • Scalability: The platform scales to 100,000+ nodes.
  • Agent Accessibility: The Netdata Agent is open source.
  • Unification: Netdata Cloud unifies and correlates data from distributed hubs.
  • Proactive Identification: Anomaly detection can identify issues before they become outages and steer engineering responses.

#Netdata #Observability #Monitoring #AI #DistributedSystems

Source: netdata/netdata

item.title: Quad9 Withdraws Public DNS Resolver from France Following Court Ruling
item.description:
Quad9 Withdraws Public DNS Resolver from France Following Court Ruling

Last month, the Swiss non-profit foundation Quad9 announced that it will withdraw its free public DNS resolver from France. This decision followed months of litigation and a French court ruling that imposed daily financial penalties on Quad9 for failing to block domains associated with alleged copyright infringement.

🔍 Overview

The French court’s ruling forced Quad9 to choose between crippling litigation and financial penalties, or fundamentally altering its service in a way that would undermine the privacy and security of its users. Left with no good option, Quad9 is choosing to withdraw its service. This withdrawal deprives French Internet users of a trustworthy tool and creates a real risk of disruption to their daily lives.

🧩 How it works

DNS resolvers are a foundational piece of the Internet’s infrastructure.

  • Address Translation: When a user types a website name, the DNS system translates that domain name into the IP address the device needs to connect.
  • Resolution: A DNS resolver looks up that address and sends it back to the device, functioning like an operator finding a phone number in a directory.
  • Blocking Limitations: The only way a DNS resolver can block content is by declining to return the IP address for a particular website. It cannot remove the actual infringing content from the Internet, nor can it take down the servers hosting it.

⚙️ Key details

Multiple public DNS resolvers are utilized globally, but they are increasingly facing regional legal pressures:

Resolver Name Provider Details
9.9.9.9 Quad9 Withdrawing from France; used by government bodies, educational institutions, hospitals, and utilities.
1.1.1.1 Cloudflare Launched in April 2018 as a fast, reliable, privacy-first consumer DNS service that does not collect or sell user data.
8.8.8.8 Google One of the best-known public resolvers.
OpenDNS Cisco Previously withdrawn from France, Portugal, and Belgium (temporarily) under similar circumstances.

💡 Why it matters

If affected parties in France do not change their resolver before Quad9 removes its service, their Internet will fail with no explanation. Quad9 has no way to directly notify these users that their resolver will soon stop working.

This challenge is part of a broader trend. A Belgian court recently issued an order that would impose substantial penalties if Cloudflare, Google, and Cisco do not begin blocking websites through their public resolvers by early January 2027. Cloudflare, which has spent years advocating against orders of this kind, has raised concerns that unrelenting demands for blocking by public DNS resolvers will end up causing real harm to the Internet.

#DNS #InternetInfrastructure #Quad9 #Cloudflare #InternetPrivacy

Source: Quad9’s withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine

item.title: Rust SDK Adds Stable 2026-07-28 MCP Version with New Features
item.description:
Rust SDK Adds Stable 2026-07-28 MCP Version with New Features

This release brings the stable MCP 2026‑07‑28 specification to the Rust SDK, while remaining fully compatible with the 2025‑11‑25 release and earlier versions.

🔍 Overview

  • The SDK implements the stable MCP 2026-07-28 specification.
  • It remains fully compatible with the 2025-11-25 release and previous versions.

🧩 Features

  • Server discovery & negotiation
  • Transport‑neutral subscriptions
  • Long‑running tasks
  • Response caching
  • Multi‑round‑trip requests
  • Standard HTTP routing headers

⚙️ SDK Structure

  • Repository crates:
    • rmcp: core crate providing the RMCP protocol implementation
    • rmcp‑macros: procedural macro crate for generating RMCP tool implementations
  • Basic dependencies:
    • tokio
    • serde
  • JSON Schema generation (version 2020‑12):
    • schemars

📦 Installation & Setup

  • Add the latest published version: 
    1

    cargo add rmcp --features server
  • Or use the dev channel: 
    1

    cargo add rmcp --features server --git https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk --branch main

🚀 Server and Client Lifecycle

  • serve() uses the legacy MCP lifecycle:
    • The client sends initialize.
    • The server returns negotiated server information.
    • The client sends notifications/initialized.
  • Use ClientServiceExt::serve_with_lifecycle to select another lifecycle explicitly.
  • ClientLifecycleMode::Initialize is equivalent to the existing serve() behavior.
  • Discover startup does not send notifications/initialized; discovery completes startup.
  • Each subsequent request carries its protocol version, client information, and capabilities in _meta.
  • For a server, serve() waits for peer input that establishes the protocol lifecycle, such as initialize from a legacy client.
  • A stdio MCP server is normally launched by an MCP client as a child process.
  • Running the executable alone in a terminal can leave this await pending because no client has sent protocol messages yet.
  • After serve() returns, the service handles messages in the background.
  • You can run other asynchronous work, then use waiting() to wait for shutdown.
  • To cancel during startup, use serve_with_ct().

🛠️ Building a Service

  • Use ServerHandler or ClientHandler to build a service.
  • Await protocol startup, then receive a handle to the running service.

#Rust #MCP #SDK #Async #JSON

Source: modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk

item.title: Verlihub Advanced NMDC Protocol Server Supports More Than 25k Users
item.description:
Verlihub Advanced NMDC Protocol Server Supports More Than 25k Users

Verlihub is an advanced NMDC+S protocol server for Linux and Windows operating systems. It offers a high-performance solution with low RAM and CPU usage, capable of holding more than 25,000 users.

🔍 Overview

Verlihub provides high-level functionality for managing connections, hub administration, and security features. It uses epoll on Linux and Windows, and supports worker threads for slow work to maintain performance efficiency.

⚙️ Key details

  • Resource Efficiency: Low RAM and CPU usage using epoll on both Linux and Windows operating systems.
  • Capacity: Able to hold more than 25,000 users.
  • Security: Built-in TLS-encrypted connections using OpenSSL, supporting plain and encrypted users on the same port. An external TLS proxy is also supported, sending the real address of the user with the $MyIP command.
  • Database Support: Offers backup and restore functionality for MySQL or MariaDB databases.
  • Customization and Localization: Allows extending functionality via Lua scripts (including HTTP requests) and supports hub messages in many languages.
  • User and Connection Management: Handles user management with privileges, clients and connections management, and logging of user IPs and complete MyINFOs (requires Ledokol).
  • GeoIP Integration: Tracks the GeoIP country, city, and ASN of users using MaxMindDB.
  • Statistics: Generates statistics for your hub (requires Ledokol).

🚀 Availability

Verlihub builds on Windows with MinGW-w64, with dependencies and build steps detailed in Install.md. TLS support is built-in using OpenSSL and enabled by default; to build without it, the -DUSE_TLS=OFF flag can be used.

Several resources are available for support and integration:

  • Website: https://github.com/verlihub
  • Wiki: https://github.com/verlihub/verlihub/wiki
  • Crash: https://crash.verlihub.net
  • Translate: https://explore.transifex.com/feardc/verlihub
  • Ledokol: https://ledo.feardc.net
  • MMDB: https://ledo.feardc.net/mmdb
  • Support: nmdcs://hub.verlihub.net:7777
  • Hublist: https://te-home.net/?do=hublist

#Verlihub #NMDC #ServerSoftware #OpenSource #Networking

Source: Verlihub/verlihub

item.title: Private VPC Connectivity for Amazon Quick Enterprise Data Sources
item.description:
Private VPC Connectivity for Amazon Quick Enterprise Data Sources

Amazon Quick now supports private connections to on‑premises data sources, letting enterprises keep regulated data behind firewalls while still using AI‑powered search, analytics, and automation.

🔍 Overview

  • Amazon Quick is an AI‑powered workspace that brings search, analytics, research, and automation into a single conversational experience.
  • When enterprise data sits behind a corporate firewall or in a private on‑premises data center, there is no direct network path from AWS, even though the AI agents and dashboards in Amazon Quick can query virtually any data source.
  • Regulatory frameworks such as HIPAA, FedRAMP, and PCI‑DSS often mandate that sensitive data remain within controlled network boundaries.

🛠️ How it Works

  • Requires an existing AWS Direct Connect or Site‑to‑Site VPN linking the on‑premises environment to the VPC.
  • Configure VPC endpoints powered by AWS PrivateLink so Quick reaches private resources over the AWS backbone.
  • Layer security groups and VPC endpoint policies for defense in depth.
  • Data‑fetching traffic (when Quick reaches into your network) travels through the VPC connection, never over the public internet.

📊 Supported Data Sources

Source Type Example Databases Connection Method
On‑premises relational databases PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, and others Queried by Amazon Quick Sight through ENIs placed in the VPC (heaviest consumer of VPC connections)
Knowledge‑base source (VPC‑only) Amazon Redshift Supported VPC connection for Quick Index
Other knowledge sources (no VPC) Confluence, SharePoint, Box, Google Drive, OneDrive, Amazon S3 Cannot use a Quick VPC connection today (but S3 bucket access can be restricted via a VPC endpoint bucket policy)

⚙️ Automation Features with Private Connectivity

  • Quick Agents underpin all conversational interactions and can invoke action connectors directly; traffic to privately hosted MCP servers or internal APIs flows through the VPC connection.
  • Quick Flows handle repeatable tasks; they invoke action connectors, including MCP servers in the VPC.
  • Quick Automate handles complex, multi‑system orchestration with human‑in‑the‑loop; any workflow calling an internal API routes through the VPC path.
  • Quick Apps inherit the same VPC connectivity as Quick Sight and Flows for interactive web applications.
  • Quick Spaces organize content but do not initiate their own data connections.

🚀 Availability & Requirements

  • An active AWS account with an Amazon Quick Enterprise subscription (VPC connections require Enterprise edition).
  • An existing VPC in the AWS Region where Quick is deployed.
  • Direct Connect or Site‑to‑Site VPN already established.
  • Quick website VPC endpoints are not available in the AWS China Regions or the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Enables enterprises to keep regulated data within controlled network boundaries while still leveraging AI‑driven search, analytics, and automation.
  • Provides a private, AWS‑backbone path that avoids the public internet, meeting compliance mandates such as HIPAA, FedRAMP, and PCI‑DSS.
  • Offers defense‑in‑depth security through VPC endpoint policies and security groups.

#AWS #AmazonQuick #VPC #EnterpriseAI #DataSecurity

Source: Securing Quick access from corporate networks with AWS PrivateLink | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Python Web UI for Mobile File Editing Built with Codex Remote and GPT-6
item.description:
Python Web UI for Mobile File Editing Built with Codex Remote and GPT-6

I built a Python web app on my phone using Codex Remote and GPT-6 Astra Extra High to view and edit files in a folder without routing credentials through the LLM.

🔍 Overview

  • Project created on 12th October 2026 from a phone.
  • Goal: edit a credentials file directly, avoiding round‑tripping through the LLM.
  • Result: a web UI for browsing and editing files in a folder.

🛠️ How it works

  • Codex Remote and GPT‑6 Astra Extra High generated the Python web app.
  • The app runs over a Tailscale network, allowing an agent to start it and a phone to connect securely.
  • File browsing interface is provided (see image).
  • Editing is powered by CodeMirror 6.
  • Monaco was considered but was rejected because it lacks a great mobile experience.

⚙️ Key details

  • Uses Python 3.11 (as indicated by the “Hello Python 3.15, goodbye 3.10, and now I can use 3.11” note).
  • Designed for mobile use: accessible from a phone via Tailscale.
  • Credentials remain on the device; they are not sent through the LLM.

🚀 Availability

  • Intended to be launched by an agent on the Tailscale network.
  • Once running, files can be edited directly from the phone’s browser.

#Python #Codex #GPT6 #Tailscale #WebUI

Source: Release: web-edit 0.1a0

item.title: Lupa Records Milestone of 3,600 Active Gemini Capsules
item.description:
Lupa Records Milestone of 3,600 Active Gemini Capsules

Lupa has identified a significant milestone for Gemini capsules, with the count of active and accessible entries reaching 3,600. This data highlights a growing collection of capsules currently accessible to the network.

⚙️ Key details

  • There are currently 3,600 Gemini capsules known to Lupa.
  • The capsules tracked are confirmed to be both active and presently accessible.

🚀 Availability

  • The number of active capsules is projected to reach and exceed the 3,600 mark by the end of this month.

#Gemini #Lupa #GeminiProtocol
